Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Anjali Upadhya
Hon'ble Ashwani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri Kaushlendra Nath Singh and Ms. Anjali Upadhya,
learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority and learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents.

Admittedly, petitioners' land of Gata Nos. 1342 and 1351 were acquired in the year 1996 by way of a notification issued under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and such proceedings of acquisition have attained finality.

It transpires that the amount of compensation was also paid to the recorded tenure holders.

sentences.text: The petitioners after several decades came to this Court by filing in Writ C-No. 10817 of 2022 and raised a grievance that adequate compensation has not been paid and that petitioners are still in possession over the acquired land.
This Court disposed of the writ petition on 19.04.2022 directing the claim of petitioners to be examined by respondent no. 2 in the said petition.

The second respondent, consequently, has examined the petitioners' claim and rejected the petitioners'
representation vide order dated 13.03.2023, which is impugned in the present writ petition.
Learned counsel for the petitioners states that the aforesaid order is wholly arbitrary.

A perusal of the order of authority would go to show that petitioners' land was acquired vide notification issued under Section 4(1)/17 of the Land Acquisition Act, dated 06.02.1996 and the declaration under Section 6/17 was also issued on 23.02.1996.
The award of the acquired land was declared on 20.02.1997.
The land of the petitioner was undisputedly included in the said notification.
It has been pointed out that the land had vested in the authority free from all encumbrances in the year 1997 itself.
The petitioners ceased to have any right, title or interest over it and, therefore, filing of the writ petition after several decades was not maintainable.

So far as the policy for allotment of land in lieu of compulsory acquisition is concerned, the order impugned records that such policy has come into existence much later and, therefore, it cannot be given a retrospective application.

The acquisition having attained finality in the year 1997, the petitioner would not be entitled to claim either higher compensation or any benefit of allotment particularly when the land acquisition proceedings, otherwise, are not under challenge before this Court.
It is otherwise not shown that petitioners' claim are covered under the policy for allotment of land.
In that view of the matter, we find no good ground to interfere with the order of the Greater NOIDA Authority dated 13.03.2023.
Writ petition, accordingly, lacks merit and is dismissed.

Order Date :- 16.5.2023 Ashutosh  Om Prakash And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151694525/
